explanation: Shared libraries are reusable code modules in C programming that allow multiple programs to share a single copy of common routines in memory, reducing executable file sizes and enabling easy updates to library functions without recompiling programs. They are used to save disk space, improve memory efficiency, and facilitate maintenance in systems like UNIX.
example_explanation: This program prints 'Hello, world!' to the console and relies on the standard library (e.g., stdio.h). When compiled with 'gcc source.c', it uses shared libraries by default, resulting in a smaller executable file compared to 'gcc -static source.c', demonstrating how shared libraries reduce file size while linking to external code at runtime.
